source_refs.claim: Source facts in lines 58-69: average gains mix wrong-to-right, already-correct, unsteerable, and reverse-effect samples; formal reporting must include per-instance outcomes, damage, collapse, and dose/layer curves.
Source facts in lines 114-128: fixed layer may sacrifice controllability, so oracle headroom should be measured before expanding layer or dose choices.

Source facts in lines 8-15 and 61-65: model/data conditions and formal arms, seeds, budgets, metrics, thresholds, and kill conditions are frozen before results, with explicit PASS, DOMAIN_LOCAL, and INSTRUMENT_INVALID exits.

caveats: Replication remains bounded to the frozen model, corpus, evaluator, and predeclared boundary set; it is not a universal-model or deployment study.
Per-instance diagnostics remain evaluation-only and cannot become PE, credit, or threshold-tuning signals.
topic.demand_relevance: Tests the demand's minimum normalized qualification margin, weakest-view criterion, direction coherence, and explicit falsification condition that a public-development PASS may fail to replicate or depend on one exact layer/view boundary.
falsification_signals: The mean effect is positive but weakest-view performance fails, or per-instance reverse-effect/right-to-wrong rates exceed limits; classify as DOMAIN_LOCAL or instrument/control failure as applicable.
A visible public-development PASS fails independent replication, or disappears under a predeclared boundary check without positive headroom.
Only one exact layer/view boundary passes while neighboring frozen checks fail, so the cross-view causal claim is not established.
topic.hypothesis: Causal hypothesis: genuine readout-control validity will replicate across reader-fit seeds and predeclared nearby layer/view boundaries with positive headroom, while shortcut or oversteer effects will appear as per-instance sign reversals, correct-to-wrong flips, or boundary fragility.
topic.mechanism: Source facts: the corpus reports that mean steering can hide rescuable, already-correct, unsteerable, and reverse-effect samples; excessive layers or dose can damage correct inputs or collapse outputs. It also requires frozen arms, seeds, budgets, metrics, thresholds, and kill conditions. Test mechanism: a valid direction should have stable per-instance signs and a positive weakest-view margin rather than relying on one average or exact boundary.
topic.research_question: Does a preregistered reader result remain valid at the weakest view, at the per-instance level, and across independent reader-fit repetitions and predeclared boundary checks?
success_signals: The same non-random reader clears the frozen gates across independent repetitions and all held-out views with a non-negative minimum normalized margin.
Per-instance effects show coherent direction, with reverse-effect and right-to-wrong rates below frozen limits rather than a positive mean masking damage.
The result replicates under predeclared nearby layer/view checks with positive headroom and is not dependent on one exact boundary.
topic.suggested_method: Select the candidate using only a preregistered training/validation rule, then freeze the model, corpus, evaluator, reader, layer, norm cap, dose, and thresholds. Repeat reader fitting with independent seeds on an untouched held-out identity/view cross-product. Evaluate predeclared neighboring eligible layer/view boundaries at matched norm and dose, without post-result optimization. Report wrong-to-right, right-to-wrong, no-change, reverse-effect, weakest-view accuracy, calibration, Cohen's d, identity retrieval, direction coherence, and replication of the complete gate result.
topic.title: Weakest-view, per-instance, and boundary-robust replication
